answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by binding identity to optical time-of-flight triangulation. Each node pulses a laser toward a wharf receiver while syncing with a canyon beacon. Verifiers check beam arrival against an onyx optical standard to certify unique coordinates. An attacker must deploy separate physical transceivers across distinct sites rather than simulating identities. However, dense fog scatters laser pulses, occasionally rejecting authentic agents.
